items.statement: The analysis generated 126 codes, removed 39 codes that did not describe health-status outcomes, retained 87 codes, and consolidated them into 50 concepts across physical, mental, and social health.
source: Full article, Results—Assessment of comprehensiveness, paragraph 1

items.statement: All five EQ-5D-Y dimensions appeared among participants’ health concepts, but social health—communication, social interaction, friendships, and family relationships—was important to participants and was not represented by a specific EQ-5D-Y dimension.

items.statement: All healthy participants and most diseased participants proposed missing dimensions. The most frequent proposals concerned disease, social relationships, diet, sleep, and economic conditions; participants also requested broader mental-health coverage and more specific questions.
source: Full article, Results—Relevance/comprehensiveness, paragraphs 4–5

items.statement: Participants often had difficulty separating ‘looking after myself’ from ‘doing usual activities’ and proposed some of the same examples for both dimensions.
source: Full article, Results—Comprehension and interpretation, paragraph 3
Full article, Discussion, paragraph 5

items.statement: No participant reported an EQ-VAS clarity problem, but three participants were uncertain about the criteria for assigning a score. Participants also reported that the many printed numbers made the scale visually confusing.
source: Full article, Results—Relevance/comprehensiveness, final paragraph

items.statement: The EQ-5D-Y is relevant to Chinese children and adolescents and captures physical and mental health, but adding or otherwise addressing social health could improve comprehensiveness.
source: Full article, Abstract—Conclusion

items.statement: Clearer, more specific questions and broader mental-health content could improve the instrument, although participants generally understood it well.

items.statement: Children, including the youngest participant, could express views about health and the instrument when suitable prompts were used; age alone did not appear to prevent articulation.
